segments.text: I found a blank wall
behind the Harvard store
salt in the mortar moon on the door everybody said leave that gray alone so i drew a red tide
made the bricks my own a gull took flight from a silver blue wave a crooked little sun on a
sailor's grave the night watch laughed through a missing tooth then handed me a brush and a bottle
truth paint won't sink when the weather turns hard
color can sail from a splintered yard
art put a spark in the dark make a map from a scar make a flame from a mark
art let the whole town see there's a wild bright flag in the part of me they told us keep quiet
keep every heart shut but i got a blue sky and a rusted old cup art hear the seawall start
throw your color overboard
the baker brought yellow the diver brought green the kid from the ferry brought magazine dreams
we painted the cranes with impossible wings a brass fish laughing at the mayor's rings
By morning, the rain tried washing it clean, but fire-lit rivers ran down the street, and every gray corner caught some of the glow.
Like the city had a secret, it was ready to show.
It was ready to show.
No museum rope, no velvet room
Just a tide pool stage and a warehouse bloom
If the wind tears one geese from the frame
We'll paint another and sign our names
Art, float a spark in the dark
Make a map from a scar
Make a flame from a mark
Art, let the whole town see
There's a wild bright flag in the part of me
From the docks to the roofs
From the rain to the stars
We are leaving our light on the places that scar
Art, with the dawn in my heart
One last red line across the blue
are
You
